stem:
Compounds $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ have all been found in the atmosphere of one of Saturn's moons.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
The equation for the complete combustion of $\mathbf{P}$, $\text{C}_4\text{N}_2\text{(l)}$, is shown.

$$\text{C}_4\text{N}_2\text{(l)} + 4\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{N}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H = -2036\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
The enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}$, of $\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ is $-384\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculate the enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}$, of $\mathbf{P}$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
One of the products of the complete combustion of $\mathbf{P}$ is nitrogen gas, $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$.

Explain the lack of reactivity of nitrogen.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Ethyne, $\text{HCN}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ are all weak Brønsted-Lowry acids.

Explain what is meant by the term *weak Brønsted-Lowry acid*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Ethyne, $\text{HCN}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ all contain triple bonds between two atoms.

A triple bond consists of one sigma ($\sigma$) and two pi ($\pi$) bonds.

Draw a labelled diagram to show the formation of one pi ($\pi$) bond.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ can be detected in the atmosphere by infrared spectroscopy.

Identify **two** absorptions, and the bonds that correspond to these absorptions, that will appear in the infrared spectra of both $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
The flow chart shows some reactions of $\mathbf{R}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction shown in reaction 1.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the structure of $\mathbf{S}$, the organic product of reaction 2.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{T}$ can also be formed by the reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ with ammonia.

State the necessary conditions of this reaction.
